title: Distribution-aware KV warmup and pin-expiry playbook for model onboarding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a distribution-aware playbook for publishing per-model KV cache performance profiles during onboarding, including an automated pin-expiry policy and shard-aware warmup schedules. This ticket covers the policy and orchestration work needed to: 1) generate sequence-distribution signatures for new model versions; 2) publish profiles to the profile-catalog with semantic versioning and TTL; 3) create warmup schedules per shard based on sequence-quantile targeting; and 4) add an automated pin-expiry / fallback mechanism that reverts to the last-stable model when profiles age out or drift is detected.
acceptance_criteria: New model onboarding pipeline attaches a sequence-distribution signature (quantiles and cluster-id histogram) to published KV profiles
Profile-catalog supports semantic profile versions and a TTL field; profiles with expired TTL are ignored by router
Pin-expiry policy implemented: default TTL 14 days, configurable per-customer and per-model; expiry triggers graceful fallback to last-stable pinned version
Shard warmup scheduler consumes profile quantiles and produces per-shard KV prefetch plans (fast lanes for top quantiles)
Canary rollout executed on two internal customers; latency and cold-start token cost measured and show <=10% regressions versus baseline
Dashboard panels for profile age, warmup success rate, and pin-expiry events added to runtime observability
implementation_notes: Sequence-signature: compute per-model sequence length quantiles (50/75/90/95/99) and a compact cluster-hash; store as profile metadata
Profile versioning: use profile semantic tag v{model_version}+profile.{minor}; attach created_at and ttl_seconds to metadata
Pin-expiry: implement policy engine that evaluates profile_age > ttl_seconds OR drift_score > drift_threshold => trigger fallback workflow
Warmup scheduler: bake a per-shard schedule that prioritizes KV ranges used by heavy-tailed quantiles; avoid full-range prefetch to limit cost
Rollforward safety: during fallback, keep an adaptive throttle to avoid sudden capacity spikes; implement backoff on failed warmup attempts
Edge-case: models that intentionally generate long sequences (e.g., code completion) should be opt-in for extended TTLs via onboarding flag
testing_plan: Unit tests for sequence-signature extraction and profile metadata validation
Integration test: publish profile to staging catalog and verify router picks profile according to TTL and pin rules
Chaos test: simulate shard-level prefetch failures and observe fallback behavior and alerting
Canary: rollout to 5% traffic on dedicated cluster and run 72-hour comparison against baseline traces
Regression: run token-cost microbenchmarks to detect >15% cost regressions from warmup policy changes
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy profile-catalog changes to staging; validate metadata and TTL handling
2) Enable shard warmup scheduler in read-only mode for one model and collect metrics for 48h
3) Run a closed canary using internal org accounts (grafana link in comments) for two weeks
4) If canary stable, enable pin-expiry enforcement for non-critical customers, keep extended TTL for flagged customers
5) Full production rollout with rollback window and operational runbook in playbook doc
monitoring_and_alerting: New Grafana panels: profile_age, drift_score, warmup_success_rate, pin_expiry_events
Alerts: warmup_success_rate < 95% for 10m => paging to infra-oncall
Alerts: sudden increase in fallback rate (>3x baseline) => auto-rollforward hold and incident channel
SLOs: maintain 99th percentile generation latency within configured SLO during warmup transitions

2025-01-30 QA: Found edge-case where sequence clusters with heavy multimodal distributions produced noisy cluster_hash; adding 2-step clustering: coarse + stable-hash to reduce churn.
